_meta.notice: FICTIONAL DEMO DATA. These organizations and breaches are invented for local development only. They are NOT real breaches. Real published data must come only through the Phase 3 review workflow. No leaked data is stored anywhere in this project.

controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.description: Require a second authentication factor for accounts, especially privileged and remote access.

controls.name: Secret Scanning
controls.description: Automatically detect committed credentials, keys and tokens before they are exposed.

controls.name: Patch & Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Timely remediation of known-exploited and high-severity vulnerabilities.

controls.name: Least-Privilege IAM
controls.description: Grant the minimum access required and review entitlements regularly.

controls.name: Network Segmentation
controls.description: Limit lateral movement by separating networks and enforcing boundaries.

controls.name: Logging & Alerting
controls.description: Centralized logging with alerting to detect intrusions and exfiltration early.

controls.name: Recovery & Backups
controls.description: Maintain tested, offline backups to recover from destructive attacks.

breaches.summary: A fictional retailer disclosed that attackers phished an employee, reused the stolen session to reach an internal reporting tool, and exported customer order data over a common cloud service. Used here to demonstrate the data model.
breaches.lessons_for_defenders: Phishing-resistant MFA on employee accounts would have blocked the reused session. Egress monitoring would have shortened the time to detection.
breaches.what_users_should_do: Watch for card misuse, enable transaction alerts, and treat unexpected 'order confirmation' emails with caution.

attack_steps.description: Employee phished via a fake single sign-on page; credentials and session captured.
Reused valid session to access an internal reporting application.
Customer order data exported to an attacker-controlled cloud storage bucket.

breaches.summary: A fictional clinic reported a ransomware incident affecting patient records. The clinic did not state how the attackers first got in, so root cause remains Undisclosed — demonstrating the project's 'never guess' rule.
breaches.lessons_for_defenders: Prompt patching of internet-facing systems and segmented backups materially reduce ransomware impact, even when the initial vector is unknown.
breaches.what_users_should_do: Monitor for medical identity theft and review any unexpected insurance correspondence.

attack_steps.description: Suspected exploitation of an internet-facing application (vector not confirmed by the clinic).
Patient record systems encrypted; services disrupted.

breaches.summary: A fictional SaaS provider was named in reports alleging access via a leaked API key in a public code repository. The company has not confirmed the incident, so it is marked Unconfirmed with an Undisclosed record count.
breaches.lessons_for_defenders: Secret scanning on every commit and short-lived, least-privilege credentials sharply reduce the blast radius of a leaked key.
breaches.what_users_should_do: If you use the service, rotate API tokens and watch for unusual account activity.

attack_steps.description: Alleged use of a valid API key exposed in a public repository.
